findings.title: A mandatory line close to, but not on, an existing grid line crashes the solve
findings.detail: `_merge_lines` only merges a mandatory line into an existing line when the two are within 1e-10 m laterally (1e-12 m in z). Between that and about 1–3 µm, the line is kept and creates sliver cells. The solve then fails inside scikit-fem with an opaque exception instead of a clear ValueError. The 'mandatory grid lines' feature therefore only works for lines more than about 3 µm (layout mode) or 10 µm (box-stack mode) from a geometry line. The doc says the runner will pass frozen reference maximum locations, and those can sit on or near die edges (for example on an unpowered die next to a hot one). If such coordinates are rounded, they fall into this gap. The failure is loud, so no wrong number is reported silently.
findings.evidence: Toy two-die layout, GridRule(h0=2e-3, dz_max=2.5e-4), extra_lines=([4.5e-3],[3e-3+dy],None), where y = 3 mm is a die edge. dy = 5e-11 m is merged and the solve works. dy = 2e-9, 1e-8, 1e-7 and 1e-6 m all raise 'Newton iteration didn't converge up to TOL=1e-12' (skfem FacetBasis invF). dy >= 3e-6 m works. Box stack, line 1e-6 m from a source edge: same Newton failure; 1e-5 m works. A z line 1e-9 m above a layer boundary: RuntimeError 'AMG-CG did not converge'.
findings.suggested_check: Reject (clear ValueError) or snap any mandatory line closer than a stated minimum separation (e.g. 1e-3*h0) to an existing level-0 line, and add a test for it.

findings.title: Q2 Tj max is the maximum over DOFs, not over the field; near-ties are decided by round-off
findings.detail: `tj_max` and `meta['tj_max_xyz']` are taken over the top-face DOFs, as documented. On a coarse Q2 mesh the field between nodes is hotter than the hottest node. In a mirror-symmetric case, two candidate nodes differed by only 3e-11 K, so which node was reported depended on round-off rather than an exact tie. A runner that compares `tj_max_xyz` between levels or platforms must allow for this.
findings.evidence: Box stack 24x16 mm, source (5..11, 4..12) mm, h0=4e-3, dz_max=1e-3, level 0. Q2: max over DOFs 369.604 K at (8, 8) mm, but dense point_values sampling of the face gives 369.685 K at (7.6, 7.7) mm. Q1, level 0: T(6.5, 6) = 369.7474313902163 K and T(6.5, 10) = 369.74743139018665 K (y-symmetric grid); the location reported was y = 6 mm, and it jumped to (8, 8) mm at level 1.
findings.suggested_check: Document that tj_max_xyz is unique only up to solver round-off and that the Q2 nodal maximum is a lower bound on the field maximum.

findings.title: extra_lines accepts different inputs in the two modes
findings.detail: Layout mode flattens each entry with np.asarray(...).ravel(), so a scalar is accepted. Box-stack mode does `cx + list(exs)`, so a scalar entry raises TypeError. The legacy `element_order` keyword is ignored without warning when `rule` is given and `element_order` is 1, because 1 is the default and cannot be told apart from an explicit 1.
findings.evidence: F.box_stack_grid(..., extra_lines=(5e-3, None, None)) raises TypeError: 'float' object is not iterable. The same scalar is accepted by layout_grid.
findings.suggested_check: Pass box-stack extras through the same ravel as layout mode.

findings.title: Legacy box-stack grids change, and the legacy-equality test cannot catch it
findings.detail: Box-stack mode now always adds each source's centroid lines, so the legacy h0= call no longer builds the grid it used to. `test_default_rule_unchanged_counts_and_legacy_signature` compares the legacy call with the rule call, but both run through the new code, so the test cannot detect any change from the old behaviour. I checked that no experiment runner calls solve_box_stack: E006 uses solve_layout only, and its default layout grid (no extra lines, dz_max None) is unchanged. Registered evidence is therefore not affected.
findings.evidence: grep over experiments/runners: thermal_fem box-stack APIs are used only in unit tests; e006_run.py and e006_f5_dev.py call FEM.solve_layout with zrefine=False and no extra_lines.

independent_checks_performed: Ran all definition-of-done commands: the 4 pytest files (61 passed), the inline API assertion (no output, no error), ruff check src tests (clean) and mfos gate --fast ('all gates passed').

Nodal values: on 200 random DOFs of Q1 and Q2 box-stack solutions, node_value equals res.T exactly and agrees with the independent FE interpolation (point_values) to 3e-13 K. This confirms that ElementHex2 mid-node DOFs are nodal temperatures, so 'node-only values' is sound for Q2.

Tj-max location: compared tj_max and tj_max_xyz with a dense 61x81 point_values sampling of the source face. For Q1 they match exactly. For Q2 the nodal maximum is 0.08 K below the field maximum at level 0.

Layout mode with two dies of different thickness and attach thickness, a mandatory z line inside the attach band, and mandatory x/y lines, levels 0–2: dz <= dz_max/2^l holds, every axis nests and bisects (a1.size == 2*a0.size-1, old lines kept), tj_max_xyz z equals each die's own top face (4.34 mm and 4.48 mm), and energy balance is about 1e-14.
On the same layout, node_value without z on the thinner die raises ValueError, because z defaults to the global top face. It works with an explicit z and at the interior mandatory z plane.
Generator layout (seed 20261103), dz_max = 2.5e-4: max dz is 2.5e-4 at level 0 and 1.25e-4 at level 1, so the bound holds.

Adversarial near-coincident mandatory lines: swept the offset from a die/source edge from 5e-11 m to 3e-4 m in layout and box-stack modes, plus z offsets from 1e-9 m to 1e-5 m. Crashes in the 2e-9 to 1e-6 m range (major finding above).

Checked that the tests are not circular: the dz counts are rebuilt independently from the stack bands, the Tj-max node is selected independently from node coordinates, and the off-node cases do raise. I also confirmed that the legacy-equality test is tautological with respect to old behaviour.
Checked whether the box-stack change reaches registered evidence: the E006 runners use only solve_layout with default extra_lines and dz_max, so their grid is unchanged.
caveats: Mandatory grid lines work only when each line is either within 1e-10 m of an existing level-0 line (1e-12 m in z) or more than about 3 µm away laterally in layout mode (10 µm in box-stack mode; more than about 1e-7 m in z). Lines in between make the solve fail with an exception; no wrong value is reported silently.

Tj max and its coordinates are the maximum over DOFs of the die top face. For Q2 on coarse grids this is below the maximum of the FE field (by 0.08 K in the case I checked). On symmetric problems the reported coordinate is decided by round-off between near-equal nodes.
node_value's default z is the global top face. For a die thinner than the thickest one, z must be passed explicitly (it raises otherwise, which is correct but easy to trip over).
Box-stack grids now always include source centroid lines, so legacy box-stack results differ from earlier ones. No registered experiment runner uses box-stack mode.
